body: I can fix compile.sh by throwing in some "s, but the resulting Bazel won't actually build things (as it does not allow spaces in paths to runfiles).  Let me see if we can fix that, but for now, can you use a path without spaces in it?

Thanks. I am now using a path without spaces, and it's working fine now.

As a suggestion, it would be good to clarify somewhere (e.g. the "Installing Bazel" page or in the script) that bazel currently does not work for paths with spaces.

issue.title: Bazel getting stuck while building

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
I've been having trouble  building things with Bazel lately. The issue manifests itself with Bazel appearing to be stuck (with no CPU load) at essentially random build steps (including the loading and analysis phase). This happens both when I attempt to build targets from my own repository, as well as in the bootstrap step in the Bazel installation; I've also tried with releases 0.1.0 and 0.1.2 with no success this far.

For example, when running `./compile.sh` from HEAD just now I get stuck with the following (aborted after several minutes without any progress):

``` sh
[mnett@singularity ~/Development/bazel] (master) Sat Jan 02 22:40:25 $ ./compile.sh                                                                                    
INFO: You can skip this first step by providing a path to the bazel binary as second argument:                                                                         
INFO:    ./compile.sh build /path/to/bazel                                                                                                                             
🍃  Building Bazel from scratch............                                                                                                                             
🍃  Building Bazel with Bazel.                                                                                                                                          
.Extracting Bazel installation...                                                                                                                                      
Sending SIGTERM to previous Bazel server (pid=26879)... done.                                                                                                          
.......                                                                                                                                                                
INFO: Found 1 target...                                                                                                                                                
[2 / 45] Writing file src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/libbazel-main.jar-2.params
```

If I interpret the output of `strace` (see below), this seems to be a deadlock.

``` sh
[mnett@singularity ~] Sat Jan 02 22:40:58 $ sudo strace -p 26879
[sudo] password for mnett: 
Process 26879 attached
futex(0x7f059b3319d0, FUTEX_WAIT, 26880, NULL) = ? ERESTARTSYS (To be restarted if SA_RESTART is set)
--- SIGTERM {si_signo=SIGTERM, si_code=SI_USER, si_pid=30672, si_uid=1000} ---
futex(0x7f059a5028c0, FUTEX_WAKE_PRIVATE, 1) = 1
rt_sigreturn()                          = 202
futex(0x7f059b3319d0, FUTEX_WAIT, 26880, NULL <unfinished ...>
+++ exited with 143 +++
[mnett@singularity ~] Sat Jan 02 22:45:38 $ sudo strace -p 30715
Process 30715 attached
futex(0x7f50b497b9d0, FUTEX_WAIT, 30716, NULL
```

The step at which the deadlock happens seems arbitrary and repeatedly running a build command eventually succeeds. Anyway, I didn't find any issues that seem to be related to this, and at this point I'm unsure of how to further debug the problem.

Do you have any suggestions?

issue.title: Enable spaces in exports_files

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
We put a binary Python archive in an external repo.

For that repository we had the `BUILD` file:

```
all_files = glob(["**"])

exports_files(srcs=all_files)
```

which is making Bazel complain about a target having a space (setuptools has a file with spaces in basename). Which I understand as a limitation for targets, but it is not always an option to remove paths with spaces from thirdparty libraries.

issue.title: Java source file name may not contain '$'?

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
/CC @damienmg @spearce

I'm trying to implement Bazel build for Gerrit Code Review project [prolog-cafe](https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/#/admin/projects/prolog-cafe), that is currently built with Buck and Bucklets.

And facing the problem, that source files contains '$':

```
java_library(
  name = 'lang',
  srcs = glob([
      SRC + 'exceptions/*.java',
      SRC + 'lang/*.java',
    ],
    exclude = REPL),
)
```

Build doesn't work at all:

```
$ bazel query --output=build :lang
ERROR: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:51:1: //:builtin: invalid label 'java/com/googlecode/prolog_cafe/builtin/PRED_$atom_type0_2.java' in element 0 of attribute 'srcs' in 'java_library' rule: invalid target name 'java/com/googlecode/prolog_cafe/builtin/PRED_$atom_type0_2.java': target names may not contain '$'.
WARNING: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:60:1: target 'builtin_srcs.am' is both a rule and a file; please choose another name for the rule.
WARNING: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:66:1: target 'system_srcs.am' is both a rule and a file; please choose another name for the rule.
ERROR: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:66:1: Label '//:src/builtin/system.pl' is duplicated in the 'srcs' attribute of rule 'system_srcs.am'.
WARNING: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:81:1: target 'io_srcs.am' is both a rule and a file; please choose another name for the rule.
WARNING: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:100:1: target 'pl2am_srcs.am' is both a rule and a file; please choose another name for the rule.
ERROR: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:100:1: Label '//:src/compiler/pl2am.pl' is duplicated in the 'srcs' attribute of rule 'pl2am_srcs.am'.
WARNING: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:106:1: target 'am2j_srcs.am' is both a rule and a file; please choose another name for the rule.
ERROR: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:124:1: //:cafeteria_lib: invalid label 'java/com/googlecode/prolog_cafe/builtin/PRED_$write_toString_2.java' in element 2 of attribute 'srcs' in 'java_library' rule: invalid target name 'java/com/googlecode/prolog_cafe/builtin/PRED_$write_toString_2.java': target names may not contain '$'.
WARNING: /home/davido/projects/prolog-cafe/BUILD:134:1: target 'cafeteria_srcs.am' is both a rule and a file; please choose another name for the rule.
ERROR: error loading package '': Package '' contains errors.
```

Now I'm wondering how this library is built at Google with Blaze?

Here is the `BUILD` file: [1], and here is the `prolog.bzl` fie content: [2].

After some investigation, I see, that the problem is not `java_library`, but `genrule` implementation that generate java from prolog code. After rmoving those generic rules, `:lang` can be built. So that needs further investigations:

```
davido@linux-ucwl:~/projects/prolog-cafe (master %=)$ bazel build :lang
INFO: Found 1 target...
INFO: From Building liblang.jar (48 source files):
Note: Some input files use unchecked or unsafe operations.
Note: Recompile with -Xlint:unchecked for details.
Target //:lang up-to-date:
  bazel-bin/liblang.jar
INFO: Elapsed time: 3.965s, Critical Path: 1.34s

```

* [1] http://paste.openstack.org/show/597134/
* [2] http://paste.openstack.org/show/597135/

body: Closing this issue in favor of #374 that is more precise.
